title: Pennsylvania will require labels on AI-generated ads
slides: Will Pennsylvania's AI ad labels change political persuasion?
The state now mandates disclosure on synthetic political ads.
But the rule targets only ads, not organic posts or memes.
Campaigns must audit every creative for AI-generated content.
Check your own feeds—will labels reach you before November?
thread_text:
1. Labels only on ads?

Pennsylvania now requires disclosure on synthetic political ads. But organic posts and memes? Completely exempt.

2. Loophole you can drive through

A campaign can post the same AI-generated message organically and skip the label entirely. The rule only covers paid ads.

3. Campaigns must audit everything

Every creative needs a check for AI-generated content before it goes live. One missed audit could mean a fine or forced takedown.

4. You won't see it coming

Most political content you share isn't a paid ad. It's a post from a friend or a page you follow. Labels won't appear there.

5. Check your own feed

Before November, scroll your feed and ask: how many posts would need a label if they were ads? Test it this week.

instagram.caption:
If you run a political ad in Pennsylvania, the state now requires you to label it if any part was made with AI. 🗳️

The rule only covers paid ads. Organic posts and memes can spread the same synthetic message with no label at all.

Campaigns also have to audit every piece of creative for AI content before it goes live—one missed check can mean a fine or a forced takedown.

So most political content you actually share—a post from a friend or a page you follow—won't carry any label. 🤔

Before November, scroll your feed and count how many posts would need a label if they were ads. 📱
